page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Expose the minimum configuration surface needed to understand and operate Scenario to Android safely — signing identity references, default transport preference, and locale.

priorities.statement: Signing material is referenced by identity and never displayed.
priorities.notes: The upload keystore lives in secrets-manager. This surface shows which identity is configured, never its value.

priorities.statement: A configured-but-unresolvable secret reference reads as an error, not as configured.
priorities.notes: A dangling reference that renders as satisfied is how a build fails at signing time with no prior warning.

priorities.statement: The default transport for release-relevant runs is visible and defaults to USB.
priorities.notes: Wireless pairing expires on reboot; silently defaulting to it makes transport faults present as failed conformance chapters.

elements.name: Signing identity
elements.description: The secrets-manager identity used for signing, shown as a reference only.

elements.name: Default transport
elements.description: The transport used for release-relevant runs, defaulting to USB.

states.description: Configuration is being fetched; no values are asserted yet.
Nothing has been configured yet. Explains what each setting affects rather than showing blank fields.
Some settings are configured and others are not; unset values are explicitly unset rather than defaulted silently.
Displayed configuration may not match the running service because a reload is pending.
Configuration could not be loaded or saved. The failure is reported with what is still safe to do.
A signing identity is configured but cannot be resolved in secrets-manager. Reads as an error, not as configured.

claims.statement: The configured signing identity is present as a reference on the settings surface.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-007. An operator must be able to see which identity is in use without the surface ever rendering key material.

claims.statement: The transport used for release-relevant runs is visible in settings.
claims.rationale: S2A-P1-001. Wireless flakiness presents as failed conformance chapters, so which transport is in use must not be invisible.

claims.statement: An unresolvable signing reference renders distinguishably from a resolvable one.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-007. A dangling reference that reads as configured produces a build that fails at signing with no prior warning.

claims.statement: No keystore, private key, password, or service-account key value appears anywhere on this surface in any state.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-007. Absence of secret material cannot be proven from the accessibility tree alone — a value could render as ordinary text — so this needs human attestation backed by a source-level check.
